339: /** Apply every opcode in a batch to the DOM (TREE structure + PARAMETER/META deltas). */
340: export function applyBatch(batch: Batch, renderer: DomRenderer): void {
341:   // SSR snapshot fit slots (`data-pathland-fit-cands`) touched by a structural
342:   // removal in this batch. The gate is torn down AFTER the whole batch, gated on
343:   // the slot's FINAL state (issue #141): a removal that does NOT reduce the slot
344:   // to a single live candidate (e.g. a band-crossing fit swap dropping a child
345:   // inside a candidate) must leave the gate intact — unwrapping it eagerly would
346:   // expose every candidate (the "all branches rendered" bug).
347:   const touchedFitGates = new Set<HTMLElement>();
348:   for (let i = 0; i < batch.opcodes.length; i++) {
349:     const op = batch.opcodes[i]!;
350:     try {
351:       switch (op.category) {
352:         case CAT_TREE:
353:           applyTree(op, renderer, touchedFitGates);
354:           break;
355:         case CAT_PARAMETER:
356:           applyStyle(op, batch.strings, renderer);
357:           break;
358:         case CAT_META:
359:           applyMeta(op, renderer);
360:           break;
361:         default:
362:           break;
363:       }
364:     } catch (err) {
365:       // The batch is a renderer-consuming instruction stream; an empty catch
366:       // would hide a structural bug. Log the exact op for remote diagnosis,
367:       // then rethrow (the host's handleMessage surfaces it).
368:       const el = renderer.byId.get(op.a);
369:       const where = el instanceof Element
370:         ? `${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}#${el.getAttribute("data-pathland-id")}.${el.className}`
371:         : String(el);
372:       console.error(
373:         `[pathland] applyBatch failed at op ${i}/${batch.opcodes.length} ` +
374:         `cat=${op.category} cmd=${op.command} a=${op.a} b=${op.b} c=${op.c} target=${where}`, err);
375:       throw err;
376:     }
377:   }
378:   for (const slot of touchedFitGates) {
379:     reconcileFitGate(slot);
380:   }
381:   // Derived layout (fill propagation, ZStack sizing/positioning, cross-axis
382:   // align-self) — mirrors the Rust SSR renderer's whole-tree decisions.
383:   applyLayout(renderer);
384: }

387:   switch (op.command) {
388:     case CMD_RESET: {

390:         if (el.parentNode) {

392:         }
393:       }

396:     }

403: /** The node actually inserted into a parent's container: ZStack children are
404:  *  wrapped in a `grid-area:1/1` cell shell, grid cells (a GRID's bare children
405:  *  or a GRID_ROW's children) in an auto-placed cell shell (the layout pass sets
406:  *  their `justify-self`/`align-self` and explicit `grid-row`/`grid-column` from
407:  *  the container's structure/ALIGNMENT — mirrors the Rust SSR renderer), a
408:  *  GRID_ROW itself inserts directly (it is the row container, not a cell);
409:  *  everything else inserts directly. */
410: function placedChild(parent: Node, child: Node): Node {
411:   if (child instanceof HTMLElement) {
412:     const parentComp = componentByNode.get(parent);
413:     if (parentComp === COMPONENT_ZSTACK) {
414:       const wrapper = document.createElement("div");
415:       wrapper.style.gridArea = "1/1";
416:       wrapper.appendChild(child);
417:       return wrapper;
418:     }
419:     if (isGridComponent(parentComp) || parentComp === COMPONENT_GRID_ROW) {
420:       if (componentByNode.get(child) === COMPONENT_GRID_ROW) {
421:         return child; // a row container is a grid child, not a cell
422:       }
423:       const wrapper = document.createElement("div");
424:       wrapper.appendChild(child);
425:       return wrapper;
426:     }
427:   }
428:   return child;
429: }

455: function applyTree(op: Opcode, r: DomRenderer, touchedFitGates: Set<HTMLElement>): void {
456:   // N→1 fit-slot reconcile (issue #141): the server's SSR snapshot carried EVERY
457:   // candidate behind CSS `@container` gated wrappers (`data-pathland-fit-cands`).
458:   // The downgrade to a single selected child is signalled by REMOVING a candidate
459:   // (a `REMOVE_CHILD`/`DELETE_NODE` on the slot). Record the touched slot and
460:   // reconcile it AFTER the batch (`reconcileFitGate`), once the REMOVE/DELETE
461:   // deltas have applied: only a slot that actually ended up with a single live
462:   // candidate is the downgrade — a removal that merely drops a child inside a
463:   // candidate (a band-crossing fit swap) must leave the gate intact. An
464:   // `INSERT_CHILD`/`CREATE_NODE` is never the downgrade: a `META::RESYNC` replays
465:   // the whole tree and the SSR gate must SURVIVE it (the CSS band keeps showing the
466:   // width-correct candidate).
467:   if (op.command === CMD_REMOVE_CHILD || op.command === CMD_DELETE_NODE) {
468:     const slot = nearestGatedFitSlot(op, r);
469:     if (slot) {
470:       touchedFitGates.add(slot);
471:     }
472:   }
473:   switch (op.command) {
474:     case CMD_CREATE_NODE: {
475:       // Hydration-aware: an id already present in the registry is the SSR-hydrated
476:       // element — reuse it (a resync/full snapshot replays CREATE for every node
477:       // without clobbering the visible DOM). Only create a fresh shell when absent.
478:       let el = r.byId.get(op.a);
479:       if (!el) {
480:         el = createElement(op.b);
481:         if (el.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE) {
482:           (el as HTMLElement).setAttribute("data-pathland-id", String(op.a));
483:         }
484:         r.byId.set(op.a, el);
485:       }
486:       if (el.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE) {
487:         componentByNode.set(el, op.b);
488:       }
489:       break;
490:     }
491:     case CMD_DELETE_NODE: {
492:       const el = r.byId.get(op.a);
493:       if (el) {
494:         const host = el as HTMLElement;
495:         // `DELETE_NODE` covers the whole subtree: every descendant's registry
496:         // entry must die too, or a later op could reuse a still-registered
497:         // (detached) element and double-parent it (HierarchyRequestError).
498:         purgeSubtreeRegistry(host, r);
499:         if (host.parentNode) {
500:           host.parentNode.removeChild(host);
501:         }
502:       }
503:       r.byId.delete(op.a);
504:       break;
505:     }
506:     case CMD_INSERT_CHILD: {
507:       const child = r.byId.get(op.b);
508:       const parentNode = r.byId.get(op.a);
509:       if (!child || !parentNode) {
510:         break;
511:       }
512:       let parent: Node = parentNode;
513:       // A media node gaining custom control children morphs its bare media
514:       // element into a `.pathland-media` wrapper (the Rust SSR emits the same
515:       // structure); the children then attach to the wrapper.
516:       const comp = componentByNode.get(parentNode);
517:       if ((comp === COMPONENT_AUDIO || comp === COMPONENT_VIDEO)
518:           && parentNode instanceof HTMLElement && parentNode.matches("audio,video")) {
519:         parent = mediaToWrapper(parentNode, r);
520:       }
521:       const container = childrenContainer(parent);
522:       // Hydration/idempotent-replay guard: skip when the child is already there
523:       // (the SSR DOM already holds the initial tree; a resync replays it), or
524:       // when a duplicate of the node already exists by id (drift protection —
525:       // never render a second copy the app did not emit).
526:       if (container && !container.contains(child)
527:           && !(child instanceof Element && container instanceof Element
528:             && container.querySelector(`[data-pathland-id="${op.b}"]`))) {
529:         let placed = placedChild(parent, child);
530:         if (comp === COMPONENT_PICKER && child instanceof HTMLElement) {
531:           // Picker children are option labels → materialize native `<option>`s.
532:           placed = pickerOption(child);
533:           r.byId.set(op.b, placed);
534:           componentByNode.set(placed, COMPONENT_TEXT);
535:         }
536:         insertAt(container, placed, op.c);
537:         if (comp === COMPONENT_PICKER) {
538:           renumberPickerOptions(container);
539:         }
540:         maybeAnimateInsert(parent, placed);
541:       }
542:       break;
543:     }
544:     case CMD_REMOVE_CHILD: {
545:       const child = r.byId.get(op.b);
546:       if (child && child.parentNode) {
547:         child.parentNode.removeChild(child);
548:       }
549:       break;
550:     }
551:     case CMD_MOVE_CHILD: {
552:       const child = r.byId.get(op.b);
553:       if (!child) {
554:         break;
555:       }
556:       const parent = r.byId.get(op.a);
557:       if (parent) {
558:         const container = childrenContainer(parent);
559:         if (container) {
560:           // Detach the child (and its now-empty ZStack wrapper, if any) so the
561:           // wrapper-count stays in sync with the Rust SSR structure.
562:           const oldParent = child.parentNode;
563:           child.parentNode?.removeChild(child);
564:           if (
565:             oldParent instanceof HTMLElement &&
566:             oldParent !== container &&
567:             oldParent.childElementCount === 0 &&
568:             oldParent.style.position === "absolute"
569:           ) {
570:             oldParent.remove();
571:           }
572:           let placed = placedChild(parent, child);
573:           if (componentByNode.get(parent) === COMPONENT_PICKER && child instanceof HTMLElement) {
574:             placed = pickerOption(child);
575:             r.byId.set(op.b, placed);
576:             componentByNode.set(placed, COMPONENT_TEXT);
577:           }
578:           insertAt(container, placed, op.c);
579:           if (componentByNode.get(parent) === COMPONENT_PICKER) {
580:             renumberPickerOptions(container);
581:           }
582:         }
583:       }
584:       break;
585:     }
586:     default:
587:       break;
588:   }
589: }

591: function insertAt(container: Node, child: Node, index: number): void {
592:   // Inserting a node into itself or its own subtree yields an incorrect node
593:   // tree — the child is effectively already positioned; skip (never throw).
594:   if (child === container || container.contains(child)) {
595:     return;
596:   }
597:   // The protocol's INSERT/MOVE index counts ELEMENT children. Debug-comment
598:   // nodes (`<!-- #id … -->`, `pathland.debug-html=true`) are sibling children
599:   // in the SSR-hydrated DOM, so counting them in `visible` shifts every index
600:   // and e.g. would insert a trailing sidebar BEFORE the main area. Count
601:   // elements only; the injected nav-back button is excluded by class.
602:   const visible = Array.from(container.childNodes).filter(
603:     (n) =>
604:       n.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE &&
605:       !(n instanceof HTMLElement && n.classList.contains(NAV_BACK_CLASS)),
606:   );
607:   const target = visible[index];
608:   detachIfWrongParent(container, child);
609:   if (target) {
610:     if (target === child || target.contains(child)) {
611:       // Would yield an incorrect node tree (inserting a node before itself or a
612:       // descendant) — the child is already positioned; nothing to do.
613:       return;
614:     }
615:     container.insertBefore(child, target);
616:   } else {
617:     container.appendChild(child);
618:   }
619: }

622: // A `PlatformDefault` nav slot at depth > 1 gets a default back button drawn by
623: // the DOM renderer (the web has no native navigation container). The button is
624: // a tracked child of the slot that the reconcile ignores (see `insertAt`), so
625: // TREE deltas never displace it. `Custom` chrome slots never get one.

627: /** The injected default back button's class (excluded from child indexing). */

630: /** Whether an element is a nav slot (carries a `data-pathland-route`). */

632:   return el.hasAttribute("data-pathland-route");

635: /** The slot's chrome mode: `true` when the developer owns all nav UI. */
636: function isCustomChrome(el: HTMLElement): boolean {
637:   return el.getAttribute("data-pathland-nav-chrome") === "custom";

640: /** The slot's current depth (defaults to 1 = root destination). */
641: function slotDepth(el: HTMLElement): number {
642:   return Math.max(1, Number(el.getAttribute("data-pathland-depth") ?? "1") || 1);

645: /** The injected back button inside a slot, if present. */
646: function injectedBackButton(el: HTMLElement): HTMLButtonElement | null {

652:  * `PlatformDefault` slot at depth > 1, removed for `Custom` chrome or depth 1.
653:  * Called from `SET_PROPERTY` (depth/chrome changes) and once at hydrate.
654:  */

656:   if (!isNavSlot(el) || isCustomChrome(el) || slotDepth(el) <= 1) {
657:     injectedBackButton(el)?.remove();
658:     return;
659:   }
660:   let back = injectedBackButton(el);
661:   if (!back) {
662:     back = document.createElement("button");
663:     back.type = "button";
664:     back.className = NAV_BACK_CLASS;
665:     back.setAttribute("aria-label", "Back");
666:     back.textContent = "‹ Back";
667:     back.addEventListener("click", () => r.onNavigateBack?.());
668:     el.insertBefore(back, el.firstChild); // above the destination
669:   }

672: /** Reconcile the default back button for every nav slot in the tree (hydrate). */

675:     if (node instanceof HTMLElement && isNavSlot(node)) {

681: // --- swap transitions (spec DSL.md §4.5 / MODIFIERS.md TRANSITION) ---
682: // When a child is inserted into a slot carrying a `data-pathland-transition` hint,
683: // the DOM client animates the new subtree in (fade/slide/scale). This is a pure
684: // renderer-side animation of its own output cache — never app state.

686: const TRANSITION_KEYFRAMES: Record<string, string> = {
687:   platform: "@keyframes pl-platform { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }",
688:   fade: "@keyframes pl-fade { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }",
689:   slide:
690:     "@keyframes pl-slide { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(16px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }",
691:   scale:
692:     "@keyframes pl-scale { from { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.96); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }",
693: };

695: let transitionsInjected = false;

697: function ensureTransitionStyles(): void {
698:   if (transitionsInjected || typeof document === "undefined") {
699:     return;
700:   }
701:   transitionsInjected = true;
702:   const style = document.createElement("style");
703:   style.setAttribute("data-pathland-transitions", "");
704:   style.textContent = Object.values(TRANSITION_KEYFRAMES).join("\n");
705:   document.head.appendChild(style);

708: function maybeAnimateInsert(parent: Node, child: Node): void {
709:   if (!(parent instanceof HTMLElement) || !(child instanceof HTMLElement)) {
710:     return;

712:   const name = parent.getAttribute("data-pathland-transition");
713:   if (!name) {
714:     return;
715:   }
716:   ensureTransitionStyles();
717:   const key = TRANSITION_KEYFRAMES[name] ? name : "platform";
718:   child.style.animation = `pl-${key} 180ms ease-out`;
719:   child.addEventListener("animationend", () => {

724: /** Resolve an element's role shell kind: from the component when known (fresh
725:  *  nodes), else from its tag (SSR-hydrated nodes have no component). */
726: function shellKind(el: HTMLElement): "generic" | "native" | "other" {
727:   const comp = componentByNode.get(el);
728:   if (comp !== undefined) {
729:     if (GENERIC_COMPONENTS.includes(comp)) {
730:       return "generic";
731:     }
732:     if (NATIVE_ROLE_COMPONENTS.includes(comp)) {
733:       return "native";
734:     }
735:     return "other";
736:   }
737:   const t = el.tagName.toLowerCase();
738:   if (t === "div" || t === "span") {
739:     return el.classList.contains("pathland-menu") || el.classList.contains("pathland-stepper")
740:       ? "other"
741:       : "generic";
742:   }
743:   if (
744:     t === "button" ||
745:     t === "input" ||
746:     t === "label" ||
747:     t === "select" ||
748:     t === "textarea" ||
749:     t === "progress" ||
750:     t === "img"
751:   ) {
752:     return "native";
753:   }
754:   return "other";

757: /** Replace an element with one of a different tag (a semantic role retag),
758:  *  preserving attributes, children, and the registry entry. */
759: function morphRole(el: HTMLElement, tag: string, r: DomRenderer): HTMLElement {
760:   const fresh = document.createElement(tag);
761:   for (const attr of Array.from(el.attributes)) {
762:     fresh.setAttribute(attr.name, attr.value);
763:   }
764:   while (el.firstChild) {
765:     fresh.appendChild(el.firstChild);
766:   }
767:   if (el.parentNode) {
768:     el.parentNode.replaceChild(fresh, el);
769:   }
770:   const id = Number(el.getAttribute("data-pathland-id"));
771:   if (id) {
772:     r.byId.set(id, fresh);
773:   }
774:   const comp = componentByNode.get(el);
775:   if (comp !== undefined) {
776:     componentByNode.set(fresh, comp);
777:   }
778:   const role = roleByNode.get(el);
779:   if (role !== undefined) {
780:     roleByNode.set(fresh, role);
781:   }
782:   copyTypography(el, fresh);
783:   return fresh;

787:  *  current `ROLE` / `TEXT_STYLE` state (a heading `TEXT_STYLE` always wins).

789: function applySemantic(el: HTMLElement, r: DomRenderer): void {
790:   const kind = shellKind(el);

794:   let current = el;

796:     current = morphRole(current, tag, r);
797:   }
798:   const aria = ariaRole(kind, role);
799:   if (aria) {
800:     current.setAttribute("role", aria);
801:   } else {
802:     current.removeAttribute("role");

806: function applyStyle(op: Opcode, strings: Uint8Array, r: DomRenderer): void {
807:   if (op.command === CMD_SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) {
808:     applyDesignToken(op, strings, r.tokenSink ?? createTokenSink());
809:     return;
810:   }
811:   const node = r.byId.get(op.a);
812:   if (!node || node.nodeType !== Node.ELEMENT_NODE) {
813:     return;
814:   }
815:   const el = node as HTMLElement;
816:   switch (op.command) {
817:     case CMD_SET_TEXT:
818:       setNodeText(el, readString(strings, op.b));
819:       break;
820:     case CMD_SET_DATE: {
821:       const input = el.matches("input[type=date],input[type=time],input[type=datetime-local]")
822:         ? (el as HTMLInputElement)
823:         : el.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=date],input[type=time],input[type=datetime-local]");
824:       if (input) {
825:         if (input.type === "time") {
826:           input.value = millisToTime(op.c);
827:         } else if (input.type === "datetime-local") {
828:           const date = daysToIso(op.b);
829:           const time = millisToTime(op.c);
830:           input.value = date ? `${date}T${time}` : time;
831:         } else {
832:           input.value = daysToIso(op.b);
833:         }
834:       }
835:       break;
836:     }
837:     case CMD_SET_PROPERTY: {
838:       const propId = op.b & 0xffff;
839:       const valueType = (op.b >>> 16) & 0xff;
840:       if (valueType === VAL_STRING) {
841:         const text = readString(strings, op.c);
842:         if (propId === PROP_ROUTE) {
843:           el.setAttribute("data-pathland-route", text);
844:           r.onRoute?.(text); // host mirrors the URL (history.pushState)
845:         } else {
846:           applyStringProperty(el, propId, text);
847:           if (propId === PROP_AUDIO_SOURCE || propId === PROP_VIDEO_SOURCE) {
848:             // Wire a media node's element + listeners, finalize native controls
849:             // (a control-less media node renders native controls), and resume
850:             // playback if the app was playing (a src change pauses the element).
851:             ensureMediaElement(el, propId);
852:             applyStringProperty(el, propId, text);
853:             setupMediaElement(el, r);
854:             finalizeNativeMedia(el);
855:             resumeIfPlaying(el);
856:           }
857:         }
858:       } else if (valueType === VAL_DESIGN_TOKEN) {
859:         applyTokenRefProperty(el, propId, readString(strings, op.c));
860:       } else if (valueType === VAL_LIST) {
861:         applyFitQuery(el, r, readList(strings, op.c));

1: // WebSocket transport: connects to the server's reserved `/_pathland/ws`,
2: // applies each received PLPL batch to the DOM renderer, negotiates the protocol
3: // version, and reports raw-input events back. Reconnect/backoff, heartbeat, and
4: // sequence-gap recovery (lost batches without a disconnect → META::RESYNC) live
5: // here.

8: import { ProtocolError, parseBatch } from "./plpl";
9: import { applyBatch, type DomRenderer } from "./apply";
10: import { encodePing, encodeResync } from "./events";
11: import { FLAG_HOST_TO_GUEST, VERSION } from "./constants";
12: import { log } from "./log";
13: import { describeBatch, describeBatchDetail } from "./describe";

15: export type TransportStatus = "connecting" | "open" | "reconnecting";
16: 
17: export interface TransportOptions {
18:   /** WebSocket URL, e.g. `ws://host/_pathland/ws`. */
19:   url: string;
20:   /** The retained-node registry deltas are applied to. */
21:   renderer: DomRenderer;
22:   /** Invoked after a batch is successfully applied. */
23:   onBatch?: (batch: Batch) => void;
24:   onStatus?: (status: TransportStatus) => void;
25:   /**
26:    * Invoked on every socket open (first connect and reconnect), before any RESYNC —
27:    * the DOM client sends its `META::ENVIRONMENT` (viewport + route) here as the first
28:    * message so the server session seeds from it.
29:    */
30:   onOpen?: (transport: Transport) => void;
31:   /** Injectable socket factory (tests). */
32:   createSocket?: (url: string) => WebSocket;
33: }

35: const BASE_DELAY_MS = 500;
36: const MAX_DELAY_MS = 30000;
37: const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 30;
38: 
39: // Heartbeat (spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat): the client probes server
40: // liveness with META::PING every HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS. It treats the connection
41: // as dead when NO server batch of any kind (deltas, META::PONG) has arrived for
42: // HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS — a stalled-but-"open" socket never fires onclose, so the
43: // watchdog forces a close to trigger the reconnect flow (which re-sends the
44: // environment + requests a META::RESYNC). The PING also counts as inbound WS
45: // traffic, keeping the connection warm through proxies and idle-spin-down.
46: const HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 5000;
47: const HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000;
48: const WATCHDOG_CHECK_MS = 1000;
49:

51: const WS_OPEN = 1;
52: 
53: export class Transport {

55:   private attempt = 0;
56:   private stopped = false;
57:   private readonly options: TransportOptions;
58:   private pingTimer: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;
59:   private watchdogTimer: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;
60:   private lastActivityAt = 0;
61:   /**

67:

70:   }

131:   private stopHeartbeat(): void {

133:       clearInterval(this.pingTimer);

135:     }
136:     if (this.watchdogTimer) {
137:       clearInterval(this.watchdogTimer);

139:     }
140:   }

142:   private connect(): void {

144:     const ws = this.options.createSocket

154:       this.lastActivityAt = Date.now();

157:       this.expectedSequence = null;
158:       const reconnected = this.attempt > 0;
159:       this.attempt = 0;
160:       log.info("ws", reconnected ? "connected (reconnect)" : "connected");

166:       }
167:     };
168:     ws.onmessage = (event) => this.handleMessage(event.data);

170:       log.error("ws", "socket error");

172:     };

174:       this.ws = null;
175:       if (this.stopped) {
176:         log.debug("ws", "closed (stopped)");
177:         return;
178:       }
179:       log.info("ws", "closed — reconnecting (attempt", this.attempt + 1 + ")");
180:       this.options.onStatus?.("reconnecting");
181:       this.scheduleReconnect();
182:     };
183:   }
184: 
185:   private scheduleReconnect(): void {
186:     if (this.attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
187:       return;
188:     }
189:     const delay = Math.min(BASE_DELAY_MS * 2 ** this.attempt, MAX_DELAY_MS);
190:     this.attempt++;
191:     setTimeout(() => this.connect(), delay);
192:   }

194:   private handleMessage(data: unknown): void {
195:     // Any server batch (a delta, a META::PONG, anything) proves the connection
196:     // is alive — reset the heartbeat watchdog.
197:     this.lastActivityAt = Date.now();

199:     if (data instanceof ArrayBuffer) {

204:     } else {
205:       bytes = new Uint8Array(0);
206:     }
207:     let batch: Batch;
208:     try {
209:       batch = parseBatch(bytes);
210:     } catch (err) {
211:       if (err instanceof ProtocolError) {
212:         log.error("ws", "rejected batch:", err.message);
213:         return;
214:       }
215:       throw err;
216:     }
217:     log.info("ws", "← recv", describeBatch(batch));
218:     log.debug("ws", "← recv detail", describeBatchDetail(batch));

220:       log.warn("ws", `protocol version ${batch.version} != ${VERSION}; reloading`);

222:       return;
223:     }
224:     // Sequence gap detection (spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap detection): a
225:     // guest → host delta batch whose sequence breaks the chain means one or more
226:     // batches were lost while the socket stayed open. Do not apply the gapped
227:     // batch (its deltas assume the lost state); request a full snapshot and

229:     if (this.isSequenceGap(batch)) {
230:       log.warn(
231:         "ws",
232:         `sequence gap: expected ${this.expectedSequence}, got ${batch.sequence} — requesting RESYNC`,

234:       this.expectedSequence = null;
235:       this.send(encodeResync());

238:     this.trackSequence(batch);

240:       applyBatch(batch, this.options.renderer);
241:     } catch (err) {
242:       if (err instanceof ProtocolError) {
243:         log.error("ws", "rejected delta:", err.message);
244:         return;
245:       }
246:       throw err;
247:     }
248:     this.options.onBatch?.(batch);

251:   /**
252:    * True when a guest → host delta batch breaks the expected sequence chain.
253:    * Host → guest batches (heartbeat `PONG`, request echoes) carry sequence 0 and
254:    * are not part of the guest → host stream, so they are ignored here.
255:    */
256:   private isSequenceGap(batch: Batch): boolean {
257:     if ((batch.flags & FLAG_HOST_TO_GUEST) !== 0) {
258:       return false;
259:     }
260:     return this.expectedSequence !== null && batch.sequence !== this.expectedSequence;

264:   private trackSequence(batch: Batch): void {
265:     if ((batch.flags & FLAG_HOST_TO_GUEST) !== 0) {
266:       return;
267:     }
268:     this.expectedSequence = batch.sequence + 1;
269:   }

1: # @pathland/dom-renderer
2: 
3: The **Pathland DOM renderer** — the web client. A small, vanilla-TypeScript
4: hydration client (zero runtime dependencies) that:
5: 
6: - **Hydrates** the server-rendered DOM by `data-pathland-id`.
7: - **Decodes** self-contained `PLPL` opcode batches (bounds-checked) and applies
8:   them in place: **`STYLE` deltas** (the full property catalog — layout, text,
9:   styling, effects, semantic/control variants, plus `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` →
10:   CSS variables) and **`TREE` deltas** (create/delete/insert/remove/move —
11:   runtime structural updates without a full reload).
12: - **Reports raw inputs** back over WebSocket as `EVENT` batches — the full event
13:   catalog (pointer down/move/up, key down/up, value/text/date changed, focus/
14:   editing, submit, scroll, wheel) — guest → host (flags `0x0000`), gated by the
15:   SSR `EVENT_LISTENERS` mask.
16: - **Negotiates** the protocol version (mismatch → reload) and **reconnects**
17:   with exponential backoff.
18: 
19: Styling is **Option A**: the protocol stays renderer-agnostic; the SSR HTML
20: carries Tailwind classes (server-compiled), and runtime style deltas are applied
21: as inline style (overriding the current value), with literal colors inline and
22: semantic design tokens as CSS variables. The DOM renderer owns the bounded
23: property → style/class map (`src/classes.ts`).
24: 
25: ## Layout
26: 
27: ```
28: src/
29:   constants.ts   protocol constants (mirror spec/)
30:   plpl.ts        bounds-checked batch parse + string decode
31:   format.ts      f32/ARGB/date/float formatting
32:   elements.ts    component → DOM shell factory (TREE create)
33:   classes.ts     Option A style/state appliers (inline style + ARIA + CSS vars)
34:   apply.ts       delta application (STYLE + TREE) over the id → Node registry
35:   events.ts      guest → host EVENT encoders
36:   transport.ts   WebSocket connect/reconnect/version negotiation
37:   index.ts       bootstrap (hydrate + connect + listeners)
38: ```
39: 
40: ## Build & test
41: 
42: ```bash
43: npm ci
44: npm test          # vitest (happy-dom): codec round-trips, TREE/STYLE apply, transport
45: npm run build     # tsc --noEmit + esbuild -> dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js (IIFE, minified)
46: npm run copy-to-demos   # copy the bundle into both Java demos' static dirs
47: ```
48: 
49: ## The bundle
50: 
51: `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` is served by the Spring Boot and Quarkus demos under a
52: content-hashed name — `dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` (copied into each demo's static
53: resources by `npm run copy-to-demos`, which also prunes stale copies and writes the
54: `dom-renderer.current` pointer manifest the SSR layer reads to emit the `<script src>`).
55: The fresh URL per build busts the immutable asset cache.
56: 
57: ## Transport resilience
58: 
59: `src/transport.ts` reconnects with exponential backoff, keeps the connection
60: alive with a `META::PING`/`PONG` heartbeat + no-activity watchdog, and recovers
61: from lost deltas: a **sequence gap** (a batch whose per-stream `sequence` breaks
62: the chain) makes the client skip the gapped batch and request a full snapshot
63: (`META::RESYNC`). See `spec/OPCODE.md` §Transport heartbeat and §Sequence gap
64: detection.

1: // Lazy web-icon glyph resolution. SSR inlines every rendered icon's `<path>`
2: // in the page, so first render is fully embedded — no network, no cache
3: // dependency. The DOM client only needs glyph data when a delta asks for an
4: // `ICON_NAME` that the page has *not* embedded. Instead of shipping the full
5: // canonical catalog in the bundle (~13KB), the glyph is resolved lazily:
6: //   1. the JS memo cache (this session),
7: //   2. an already-embedded `svg.pathland-icon[data-pathland-icon=name]`
8: //      elsewhere in the page — its inner markup, zero bytes and zero network,
9: //   3. the renderer-owned `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` the host serves from
10: //      the shared Rust library (`pathland_html_icon_svg` over the C ABI — the
11: //      same source SSR inlines from), fetched once then memoized + HTTP-cached.
12: // Unknown/extension names and fetch failures resolve to the fallback glyph.
13: 
14: const cache = new Map<string, string>();
15: const inflight = new Map<string, Promise<string>>();
16: const current = new WeakMap<Element, string>();
17: 
18: /** The reserved framework root (`/_pathland` by default; relocated via the SSR page's `data-pathland-base`). */
19: function basePath(): string {
20:   return document.documentElement.dataset.pathlandBase ?? "/_pathland";
21: }
22: 
23: /** The decorative fallback glyph (a faint circle) — the renderer's `web_fallback_svg()`. */
24: export const FALLBACK_SVG = '<circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8"/>';
25: 
26: /** The inner markup of an already-embedded icon svg for `name`, if present. */
27: function embeddedGlyph(name: string): string | undefined {
28:   for (const svg of document.querySelectorAll("svg.pathland-icon[data-pathland-icon]")) {
29:     if (svg.getAttribute("data-pathland-icon") === name) {
30:       return svg.innerHTML;
31:     }
32:   }
33:   return undefined;
34: }

36: /**
37:  * Memorize every glyph the page has embedded — the SSR inlines each rendered
38:  * icon, so a name that was ever on screen is capturable without a fetch. The
39:  * seeds are DOM-only, so without this the very element being swapped would be
40:  * the only play glyph and flipping it to pause would make the return trip to
41:  * play a (cached) fetch. Skips empty/shadowed contents (a mid-fill element).
42:  */
43: function harvestEmbedded(): void {
44:   for (const svg of document.querySelectorAll("svg.pathland-icon[data-pathland-icon]")) {
45:     const name = svg.getAttribute("data-pathland-icon");
46:     if (!name || cache.has(name)) continue;
47:     const glyph = svg.innerHTML.trim();
48:     if (glyph) cache.set(name, glyph);
49:   }
50: }

52: async function fetchGlyph(name: string): Promise<string> {
53:   try {
54:     const url = new URL(`${basePath()}/icons/${encodeURIComponent(name)}.svg`, document.baseURI);
55:     const res = await fetch(url.href);
56:     if (!res.ok) return FALLBACK_SVG;
57:     const text = (await res.text()).trim();
58:     // The served file is the same markup SSR inlines: `<svg …>…inner…</svg>`.
59:     const inner = text.slice(text.indexOf(">") + 1, text.lastIndexOf("</svg>"));
60:     return inner || FALLBACK_SVG;
61:   } catch {
62:     return FALLBACK_SVG;
63:   }

66: /**
67:  * Ensure a glyph is cached for `name` (resolves to it, or the fallback on
68:  * failure/unknown). Deduplicated: concurrent callers share one fetch.
69:  */
70: export function preloadIcon(name: string): Promise<string> {
71:   const existing = inflight.get(name);
72:   if (existing) return existing;
73:   const done = fetchGlyph(name).then((glyph) => {
74:     cache.set(name, glyph);
75:     inflight.delete(name);
76:     return glyph;
77:   });
78:   inflight.set(name, done);
79:   return done;

# Pathland DOM Renderer (lib/typescript) — current client behavior

**Bottom line up front:** today's client is a **document-global singleton**. It hydrates *every* `[data-pathland-id]` in the page into one flat `Map<number, Node>`, opens exactly **one** WebSocket, and applies one opcode stream. There is **no** notion of a root container, no id namespacing, no second connection, and no per-stream scoping. A "proxy view" that interleaves a second server's subtree into one DOM will collide on all of these. Details below.

Everything is bundled by esbuild into `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` as an **IIFE** (`package.json:9`), and `src/index.ts` **auto-boots as a module side effect** — there is no exported factory to instantiate a second renderer.

---

## 1. SSR hydration

**Entry point / hydration:** `boot()` in `src/index.ts:103`, invoked either on `DOMContentLoaded` or immediately if the document is already parsed:

```ts
// src/index.ts:519-523
if (document.readyState === "loading") {
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", boot);
} else {
  boot();
}
```

**The `data-pathland-id` → DOM map** is built by scanning the *entire document* into one flat numeric map (`src/index.ts:104-107`):

```ts
const byId = new Map<number, Node>();
for (const el of document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>("[data-pathland-id]")) {
  byId.set(Number(el.getAttribute("data-pathland-id")), el);
}
```

**The shape it expects** — `DomRenderer` (`src/apply.ts:310-337`):

```ts
export interface DomRenderer {
  byId: Map<number, Node>;
  onRoute?: (path: string) => void;
  onNavigateBack?: () => void;
  tokenSink?: DesignTokenSink;
  onMediaEvent?: (batch: Uint8Array) => void;
  onFitEvent?: (batch: Uint8Array) => void;
}
```

No root pointer is stored: the registry is flat and the numeric key is the sole address. The tree's root is by **convention id `1`** (all golden fixtures and tests use `data-pathland-id="1"` as the root, e.g. `test/fixtures/ssr/counter.html:1`, and `renderFresh(bytes, 1)` in `test/ssr-conformance.test.ts:158-162`). Nothing in the client enforces or discovers that.

After building the map, `boot()` additionally hydrates side-car attributes:
- media nodes: `[data-pathland-media]` → `setupMediaElement` (`index.ts:188-190`)
- fit slots: `[data-pathland-fit]` → `hydrateFitElement` (`index.ts:200-202`)
- nav back buttons: `updateNavBackButtons` (`index.ts:233`)
- reserved framework base from `document.documentElement.dataset.pathlandBase` (`index.ts:112`; also read in `icons.ts:19-21`)

The test harness mirrors this hydration (`test/ssr-conformance.test.ts:165-173`):

```ts
function hydrate(fragment: string): DomRenderer {
  const host = document.createElement("div");
  host.innerHTML = fragment;
  const byId = new Map<number, Node>();
  for (const el of host.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>("[data-pathland-id]")) {
    byId.set(Number(el.getAttribute("data-pathland-id")), el);
  }
  return { byId };
}
```

Core element lookup casts the attribute to a number on every access, e.g. `Number(node.getAttribute("data-pathland-id"))` (`index.ts:253, 305, 332, 388`).

---

## 2. PLPL batch decode

**Decode entry point:** `parseBatch(bytes: Uint8Array): Batch` (`src/plpl.ts:34`). Called from `Transport.handleMessage` (`src/transport.ts:209`).

**Batch shape** (`src/plpl.ts:12-19`, `3-10`):

```ts
export interface Opcode { category: number; command: number; flags: number; a: number; b: number; c: number; }
export interface Batch {
  readonly version: number;
  readonly flags: number;
  readonly sequence: number;
  readonly opcodes: Opcode[];
  readonly strings: Uint8Array;
}
```

**Wire layout** (documented at `src/plpl.ts:28-33`, constants in `src/constants.ts:5-10`): a self-contained batch is

```
[magic u32=0x504c504c][version u16=1][flags u16][sequence u32][opcodeCount u32]   // 16-byte header
opcodeCount × 16-byte opcodes                                                     // category|command|flags|A|B|C
[stringsLen u32][strings…]                                                        // the "string arena" section
```

Parsing is fully bounds-checked and throws `ProtocolError` (`plpl.ts:22`) on truncation/bad magic/version (`plpl.ts:35-69`). Each opcode is read little-endian at `HEADER_SIZE + i*16` (`plpl.ts:54-64`).

**Sections:** there are exactly three — header, opcodes, and a single trailing `strings` byte blob. There is **no separate events or multiple-string section** in the batch; a batch is homogeneous. The `strings` blob holds variable-length entries that opcodes reference by *relative u32 offset*:

- `readString(strings, offset): string` — `[u32 len][utf8…]` (`plpl.ts:80-91`)
- `readList(strings, offset): number[]` — `[u32 count][f32 × count]`, used for `FIT_QUERY` (`plpl.ts:96-111`)

Events use the *same* batch envelope but carry `CAT_EVENT` opcodes and flags `0x0000` (guest→host); e.g. `eventBatch()` (`src/events.ts:41-57`). Text events put the payload in the string section (`encodeTextChanged`, `events.ts:170-191`).

---

## 3. Delta application

**Entry point:** `applyBatch(batch: Batch, renderer: DomRenderer): void` (`src/apply.ts:340`). It switches on `op.category` (`apply.ts:348-363`):

```ts
case CAT_TREE:      applyTree(op, renderer, touchedFitGates); break;
case CAT_PARAMETER: applyStyle(op, batch.strings, renderer); break;
case CAT_META:      applyMeta(op, renderer); break;
```

After the loop it reconciles touched fit-gates and runs `applyLayout(renderer)` (whole-tree derived layout, `apply.ts:378-384`).

### The id → element map and parent tracking

- **`byId: Map<number, Node>`** is the only registry (`apply.ts:311`). It is flat and keyed by the raw protocol node id.
- **Component type per node** is tracked in a separate `WeakMap` (`apply.ts:100`): `const componentByNode = new WeakMap<Node, number>();` — needed because hydrated SSR nodes have no component recorded.
- **Parents are NOT tracked as protocol state.** Parent/child relationships are derived from the actual DOM via `Node.parentElement` when needed:
  - layout: `const parent = el.parentElement` (`apply.ts:290`)
  - fit-gate collapse: `treeOpParent(op, r)` resolves the parent from `byId` + DOM (`apply.ts:1424-1435`)
- The **container an op inserts into** is `childrenContainer(parent)` (`src/elements.ts:315-328`), which routes children into composite sub-nodes (menu-items, toggle text span, textfield label span) and otherwise returns the node itself.

### TREE commands — `applyTree(op, r, touchedFitGates)` (`apply.ts:455`)

- **`CMD_CREATE_NODE`** (`apply.ts:474-490`): **hydration-aware** — if `op.a` already exists in `byId` it *reuses* the hydrated element; only when absent does it call `createElement(op.b)` (`elements.ts:42`) and set `data-pathland-id`. `op.a = node id`, `op.b = component type`.
- **`CMD_DELETE_NODE`** (`apply.ts:491-505`): removes the element and `purgeSubtreeRegistry(host, r)` (`apply.ts:1549-1576`), which deletes every descendant's `byId` entry + tears down media samplers/fit observers. Then `r.byId.delete(op.a)`.
- **`CMD_INSERT_CHILD`** (`apply.ts:506-543`): `op.a = parent id`, `op.b = child id`, `op.c = index`. Looks both up in `byId`; guards against re-insert if `container.contains(child)` OR if `container.querySelector('[data-pathland-id="${op.b}"]')` already exists (drift guard, `apply.ts:526-528`); may morph a media element to a wrapper; `insertAt(container, placed, op.c)`.
- **`CMD_REMOVE_CHILD`** (`apply.ts:544-550`): `op.b` child, removes from its `parentNode` (does **not** delete the registry entry).
- **`CMD_MOVE_CHILD`** (`apply.ts:551-585`): `op.a = new parent`, `op.b = child`, `op.c = index`.
- **`insertAt(container, child, index)`** (`apply.ts:591-619`): index counts **element children only**, excluding the injected `.pathland-nav-back` button (`NAV_BACK_CLASS`, `apply.ts:628`); skips inserting a node into its own subtree; `detachIfWrongParent` first.
- **`placedChild(parent, child)`** (`apply.ts:410-429`): ZStack/grid children get wrapped in a shell `<div>` before insertion.

### PARAMETER commands — `applyStyle(op, strings, r)` (`apply.ts:806`)

- `CMD_SET_TEXT` (`apply.ts:817`), `CMD_SET_DATE` (`apply.ts:820`), `CMD_SET_PROPERTY` (`apply.ts:837`), `CMD_SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (`apply.ts:807` → `applyDesignToken`, `tokens.ts:105`).
- `SET_PROPERTY` decodes `propId = op.b & 0xffff` and `valueType = (op.b >>> 16) & 0xff`; STRING values are read from the string section at offset `op.c`; special-cased properties (ROLE, TEXT_STYLE, NAV_DEPTH, NAV_CHROME, PROGRESS, media, etc.) are dispatched in `applyStringProperty` (`apply.ts:952`) and `applyNumericProperty` (`apply.ts:1047`).

### Root / container identification

There is **no root identification** in the client. A node becomes "the root" purely because it is the top of the DOM and is referenced by convention as id 1. There is no `data-pathland-root` attribute anywhere in the repo (searched). `META::RESET` (`applyMeta`, `apply.ts:386-401`) iterates **every** `byId` value and removes it, then `r.byId.clear()` — i.e. reset is *global*, not scoped.

### Node-id scope

**Global numeric namespace, shared by the entire document.** Ids are never namespaced, prefixed, or qualified by connection/stream. Two streams that both use id 1, 2, 3… will overwrite each other in `byId`.

---

## 4. Event sending

Event capture is a set of **document-level listeners** registered in `boot()`:

- pointerdown / pointermove / pointerout / click (`index.ts:248-353`)
- keydown / keyup (`index.ts:356-373`)
- focusin / focusout (`index.ts:383-408`)
- scroll / wheel (`index.ts:411-432`)
- change (toggle/select/color/date) (`index.ts:435-484`)
- input (slider/textfield/editor) (`index.ts:487-516`)

**How a node id is attached:** the event target is resolved to its nearest `[data-pathland-id]` ancestor, then `Number(...)` is passed as the event's target `A` field.

Two resolvers:
- `nodeOf(el): HTMLElement | null` — deepest `[data-pathland-id]` via `closest` (`index.ts:46-48`)
- `eventNodeOf(target, bit): HTMLElement | null` — walks up until it finds a node whose `data-event-listeners` mask includes `bit` (`index.ts:60-72`)

`LISTEN_*` bits are in `constants.ts:72-81`; gating via `listens(node, bit)` (`index.ts:79-88`) — absent attribute = permissive. Example (`index.ts:323-335`):

```ts
const node = eventNodeOf(target, LISTEN_POINTER_UP);
if (node && transport.open) {
  const id = Number(node.getAttribute("data-pathland-id"));
  transport.send(encodePointerUp(id, e.clientX, e.clientY, secondary));
}
```

**Encoders** (`src/events.ts`) each produce a **self-contained single-opcode PLPL batch** with `CAT_EVENT`, guest→host flags `0x0000`, `sequence = 0` (`eventBatch`, `events.ts:41-57`). Signatures include:

```ts
encodePointerDown(target, x, y, flags?): Uint8Array        // events.ts:99
encodePointerUp(target, x, y, flags?): Uint8Array          // events.ts:109
encodeKeyDown(target, keyCode, modifiers, repeat?): Uint8Array  // events.ts:116
encodeValueChanged(target, value): Uint8Array              // events.ts:128
encodeTextChanged(target, text): Uint8Array                // events.ts:170
encodeScroll(target, offsetX, offsetY): Uint8Array         // events.ts:211
encodeNavigate(url): Uint8Array                            // events.ts:223
```

**Sending:** `Transport.send(bytes: Uint8Array): void` (`src/transport.ts:95-108`) — gated on `this.open` (`readyState === 1`, `transport.ts:91-93`), best-effort logs a description, then `this.ws.send(bytes)`. The node id rides only in the opcode's `A` field; the batch carries **no connection/stream/origin tag**.

---

## 5. WebSocket lifecycle

**One `Transport` instance per page**, constructed in `boot()` (`index.ts:145`) and started with `transport.start()` (`index.ts:170`). Class: `Transport` (`src/transport.ts:53`). Options: `TransportOptions` (`transport.ts:17-33`).

**URL construction** (`index.ts:146`) — includes the per-window id and the framework base:

```ts
url: `${location.protocol === "https:" ? "wss" : "ws"}://${location.host}${base}/ws?wid=${wid}`
```

**Per-window id (`wid`)** (`index.ts:120-143`): stored under `sessionStorage["pathland.wid"]`; generated with `crypto.randomUUID()` if absent; `isReload = wid != null`. It is deliberately **never** written into the page URL (the boot code strips any stale `?wid=` via `history.replaceState`, `index.ts:137-143`; `urlHadWid` records that a stale wid was present). Test: `test/wid.test.ts`.

**On open** (`index.ts:151-168`), ordered:
1. Send `encodeEnvironment(w, h, location.pathname)` **first** (`index.ts:154`) — seeds the server session's router.
2. `refreshFitSlots(renderer)` (`index.ts:158`).
3. If `isReload || urlHadWid`, send `encodeResync()` (`index.ts:164-167`).

**On reconnect** (`Transport.connect`'s `onopen`, `transport.ts:149-167`): `reconnected = this.attempt > 0`; re-baselines `expectedSequence = null`; calls `options.onOpen` (so environment is re-sent) and, **if reconnected, sends `encodeResync()`** (`transport.ts:163-166`).

**Sequence-gap recovery** (`transport.ts:229-237`): a guest→host batch whose `sequence` breaks the chain is **not applied**; the client sends `encodeResync()` and re-baselines on the next batch. `isSequenceGap`/`trackSequence` (`transport.ts:256-269`) ignore host→guest (`FLAG_HOST_TO_GUEST`) batches.

**Reconnect/backoff** (`transport.ts:185-192`): exponential `500ms * 2^attempt` capped at 30s, max 30 attempts. `onclose` → `scheduleReconnect` (`transport.ts:173-183`).

**Heartbeat** (`transport.ts:110-129`): `META::PING` every 5s; a no-activity watchdog (15s) force-closes a stalled-but-open socket → reconnect → resync.

**Version negotiation** (`transport.ts:219-223`): mismatched batch version → `location.reload()`.

**What happens on a full snapshot:** the client does **not** special-case it. A snapshot arrives as an ordinary batch and goes straight through `applyBatch`. Because `CREATE_NODE` reuses existing hydrated elements (`apply.ts:475-485`) and `INSERT_CHILD` skips already-present children (`apply.ts:522-528`), a replayed full tree **reconciles in place** rather than replacing the DOM. There is **no "clear the tree first"** step, and the server's resync **does not emit `META::RESET`** — `PathlandSession.resync()` calls `emitter.renderFull()` (`lib/java/pathland-server-core/.../PathlandSession.java:162-165`), and `Emitter.renderFull()` re-emits `TREE + PARAMETER` for the retained tree (`lib/java/pathland-view/.../emit/Emitter.java:164-179`). Consequence: **a `META::RESET` (if ever sent) would globally wipe every registered node**, while a resync replay leaves unrelated DOM (e.g. another stream's subtree) untouched but also would not remove stale nodes that vanished server-side. The hydration-aware reconcile is asserted in `test/apply.test.ts:530-589`.

---

## 6. Namespacing / a second independent opcode stream into a nested DOM region

**There is nothing today.** Concretely, the blockers a proxy-view feature must address:

1. **One flat, document-global id map.** `byId` is built from all `[data-pathland-id]` in the document (`index.ts:105`), and `DomRenderer.byId` is a `Map<number, Node>` with no stream/connection key (`apply.ts:311`). Ids from two servers collide. No `data-pathland-root`, no id prefixing, no per-element origin attribute exists anywhere.

2. **One connection.** `boot()` constructs a single `Transport` with a single `renderer` object (`index.ts:144-170`). There is no exported function to create a second renderer bound to a nested container; `index.ts` is a side-effect bootstrap with no exports of `boot`.

3. **Module-level shared state across any instances.** Even if you called `applyBatch` twice, these are module singletons:
   - `componentByNode` WeakMap (`apply.ts:100`)
   - `roleByNode` WeakMap (`apply.ts:307`)
   - `fitState` WeakMap + `ResizeObserver`s (`apply.ts:1342`)
   - `mediaState` WeakMap + global `setInterval` samplers (`apply.ts:1229-1236`)
   - `transitionsInjected` boolean (`apply.ts:695`)
   These are keyed by element, so they'd *mostly* coexist, but the whole-tree passes are not scoped.

4. **Whole-document queries and whole-tree passes.**
   - `applyLayout(r)` iterates **every** `byId` value and infers structure from `parentElement` (`apply.ts:162-303`). If stream B's root is nested under stream A's DOM, the layout pass would treat the cross-stream DOM parent/child as a protocol relationship (`apply.ts:289-302`).
   - `refreshFitSlots` and `dropFitBandRules` query the **whole document** (`apply.ts:1380`, `apply.ts:1505`).
   - `index.ts` hydration / media / fit scans are document-wide (`index.ts:105, 188, 200`).
   - The icon resolver scans the whole document (`icons.ts:28-34, 44-49`).

5. **Duplicate-id guard is global.** `insertAt`/`INSERT_CHILD` use `container.querySelector('[data-pathland-id="${op.b}"]')` (`apply.ts:527-528`) — with colliding ids across streams this mis-detects duplicates.

6. **`CMD_RESET` is global** (`apply.ts:386-401`): clears all of `byId`, i.e. would tear down both streams.

7. **Design tokens are global.** The default token sink writes `:root` custom properties into one `<style data-pathland-tokens>` in `document.head` (`createTokenSink`, `tokens.ts:65-98`; used at `apply.ts:808`). Two apps with different themes would fight over `--pl-*` and `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`.

8. **Events carry no origin.** Captured events resolve a raw numeric id and send it over the single socket (`index.ts:253` etc.); there is no per-stream routing tag, so a click in stream B's DOM would be sent to stream A's server if the ids overlap.

9. **Navigation is global.** `onRoute` calls `history.pushState` on the page URL, and `popstate` sends one NAVIGATE (`index.ts:218-242`) — a second embedded app would drive the same browser history.

10. **`wid` is one per window/tab** (`sessionStorage["pathland.wid"]`, `index.ts:127-133`), shared by whatever connections the page opens; there is no per-stream id.

### What *could* be reused today
`applyBatch`, `parseBatch`, `Transport`, `createElement`, and `childrenContainer` are all exported and take an explicit `DomRenderer`/`Batch` argument, so a proxy feature could in principle drive a second `{ byId }` over a nested region — but the module-level WeakMaps (`componentByNode`, `roleByNode`, `fitState`, `mediaState`), the global token sink/head queries, the document-wide event listeners in `boot()`, and the hard-coded root convention (id 1) mean that a correct second stream requires either (a) id **namespacing/remapping** at ingest and scoped event routing, or (b) refactoring the renderer into an instantiable class with per-instance state and a **root element scope**. None of that exists in the current code.

---

| Bootstrap, hydration, `byId`, WS URL, `wid`, listeners, auto-boot | `src/index.ts` (boot at 103; map 104-107; URL 146; onOpen 151-168; auto-boot 519-523) |
